prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Key proposals (policy-only summary, under 500 words)

- Economy and business: Invest in green infrastructure, innovation and skills; repair EU trading ties; manage public finances to reduce debt share; expand British Business Bank; tougher action on tax avoidance; reform business rates into a Commercial Landowner Levy; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; fairer capital gains; 4% tax on FTSE-100 buybacks; priority future tax cut by raising the personal allowance.

- Jobs and work: Replace the apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants for adults (aim £10,000); expand higher vocational routes; create a Worker Protection Enforcement Authority; modernise employment status (new “dependent contractor” category); improve rights for zero-hours workers; overhaul Statutory Sick Pay; independent living wage review; expand parental leave/pay as day-one rights.

- Climate and energy: Net zero by 2045; 90% renewable electricity by 2030; 10-year home energy upgrade (free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households); zero‑carbon new homes; rooftop solar incentives; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas; ban fracking/new coal; end fossil subsidies with just transition; expand storage, interconnectors and community energy.

- Health: Right to see a GP within seven days/24 hours urgent (8,000 more GPs); stronger pharmacy role and 24/7 booking; fix NHS dentistry access; mental health hubs in every community and a professional in every school; 62‑day cancer treatment guarantee; public health measures (clean air, vaping rules, sugar levy extension); workforce retention plan; ambulance/hospital estate upgrades; patient rights charter; faster access to new medicines via EMA mutual recognition; health-led drugs policy and regulated cannabis market (18+).

- Social care: Free personal care; workforce plan, Royal College of Care Workers and a Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); cross-party funding commission; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite; portable care packages; National Care Agency and minimum standards.

- Education: Per‑pupil funding rises above inflation; repair/rebuild estates; tutoring for disadvantaged pupils; more early-years support; teacher workforce strategy and independent pay body; broaden curriculum and reform Ofsted reporting; strengthen SEND funding and create a national SEND body; reinstate maintenance grants; Young People’s Premium (16–18); return to Erasmus+.

- Families: Extend free school meals to all children in poverty; double Statutory Maternity/Shared Parental Pay (£350/week) and add a month for fathers/partners at 90% pay; childcare funding reforms; support kinship care; paid neonatal leave; simplify Child Maintenance and family court backlogs.

- Welfare and pensions: Remove the two‑child limit and benefit cap; reduce Universal Credit wait to five days; scrap bedroom tax; replace sanctions; target ending deep poverty; protect triple lock; fair treatment for 1950s‑born women; raise and widen Carer’s Allowance; disability benefit reforms.

- Crime and justice: Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and investigation of burglaries; reduce court backlogs; improve rehab and probation; new Online Crime Agency; replace PCCs with Police Boards; Hillsborough Law; domestic abuse specialists; halve offence‑to‑sentence time; youth diversion duty; tougher fraud redress; stronger EU data cooperation; modern slavery protections.

- Environment: Transform water companies into public benefit firms; ban bonuses until leaks/discharges end; tougher regulator; sewage tax and real‑time data; Clean Air Act (WHO standards); “double nature” by 2050; plant 60m trees/year; expand protected land/sea; deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; peat/heather‑burn bans; stronger marine protection.

- Food, farming and fisheries: National Food Strategy; accelerate and fund Environmental Land Management (+£1bn/yr); high import standards; EU veterinary/plant health deals; strengthen Groceries Code Adjudicator; support rural infrastructure; reduce farm pollution and inputs; fund alternative proteins; clear labelling; comprehensive Animal Welfare Bill; sustainable fisheries and trawling bans in MPAs.

- Housing: Build 380,000 homes/year (150,000 social); ten garden cities; empower councils on land value and Right to Buy; ban no‑fault evictions; three‑year default tenancies; national landlord register; abolish leaseholds and cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders; Rent‑to‑Own; end rough sleeping; local powers over second homes/short‑lets.

- Local government and connectivity: Multi‑year settlements; gigabit broadband nationwide; local control over second homes; support rural services and post office hubs; restore rural bus powers; expand Rural Fuel Duty Relief.

- Transport: Rapid EV charging rollout; reinstate plug‑in grant; 2030 zero‑emission sales; cut VAT on public charging to 5%; freeze rail fares and simplify tickets; rail electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail and accessibility; empower bus franchising and fund zero‑emission fleets; national active travel strategy; shift road budget to maintenance; reform flight taxes (focus on frequent flyers); super-tax private jets; limit short domestic flights with rail alternatives; moratorium on airport expansion.

- Culture, media, sport: Protect public service broadcasters; creative enterprise zones; Creative Europe participation; simple EU touring for artists; maintain free national museums; Anti‑SLAPP law; implement Leveson Part Two; gambling levy, ad limits, ombudsman and affordability checks; independent football regulator and stronger owners’ tests.

- Immigration and asylum: End Hostile Environment; move work/student visa policy to relevant departments; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; safe/legal routes; three‑month asylum decision target; allow work after three months; merit‑based work visas; exemptions for NHS/care workers; expand Youth Mobility; reverse family visa income hike; secure EU citizens’ status; Windrush justice; firewall on data‑sharing.

- Rights and equality: Uphold the Human Rights Act and ECHR; Race Equality Strategy; make misogyny a hate crime; flexible working rights; ban conversion practices; reform gender recognition and recognise non‑binary; Digital Bill of Rights; regulate biometrics; expand refuges/rape crisis centres; enhance disability rights and Access to Work; BSL expansion; assisted dying free vote.

- Political reform: Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16–17; cap donations; codify Ministerial Code; reform Lords; federal UK and strengthened devolution; stronger transparency on lobbying, donations and digital ads; citizens’ assemblies; electoral and ministerial transparency measures; compensation for Horizon and Infected Blood victims; protect whistleblowers.

- Defence and international: Increase defence spending toward 2.5% GDP; reverse Army cuts; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls; parliamentary votes on military action; procurement reform; deepen European/NATO/EU security cooperation; support Ukraine and seize Russian assets; restore aid to 0.7% with independent department; four‑stage plan to rebuild UK‑EU ties (including Single Market goal); human rights sanctions; ceasefire and two‑state approach for Israel‑Palestine and recognise Palestine; measures on China/Hong Kong/Uyghurs/Taiwan; fund BBC World Service; ODA focus on SDGs, education (15%), climate and nutrition.
